sentences.text: Alexandronectes was a long-necked marine reptile belonging to the elasmosaurid plesiosaur family.
The genus Alexandronectes contains only one known species, A. zealandiensis.
Alexandronectes differs from other aristonectines by having a smaller skull, distinct paroccipital processes, and a different mandibular glenoid.
Fossils of Alexandronectes were discovered in the Conway Formation of Canterbury, dating to the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous.
The fossils of Alexandronectes were discovered by Alexander McKay.
The holotype specimens are cataloged as M Zfr 73 and CM Zfr 91.
The genus and species Alexandronectes zealandiensis were formally described in 2016 by Otero et al. in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
Alexandronectes is classified in the subfamily Aristonectinae based on its pterygoid structure and an A-shaped squamosal arch.
Researchers classified Alexandronectes within the Elasmosauridae family and the Aristonectinae subfamily.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kaiwhekea is the closest relative of Alexandronectes.
The fossil range of Alexandronectes includes the Campanian stage.
